encoding.assumption: POSIX path flavour (os.name == 'posix'). pathlib.Path(file).is_absolute() consults the OS path module; on POSIX a path is absolute iff it begins with '/'. The Windows branch (PureWindowsPath) treats a drive-letter root like 'C:/...' as absolute, so the encoding is exact only under POSIX.

platform_divergence.note: C:/Program Files/AMD/ROCm/5.7/bin/clang++.exe is FALSE under PurePosixPath.is_absolute() but TRUE under PureWindowsPath.is_absolute(). Container is os.name=='posix', so the deployed/tested behavior for this value is False.

crosshair.caveat: Absence of a counterexample is NOT a proof of equivalence.

notes: Branch is a pure string predicate under the POSIX assumption that holds in-container and on the deployed Linux toolchain path. Z3 returned real sat models for both polarities over the seeded domain (TRUE=/opt/rocm/bin/amdclang++, FALSE=C:/...exe). Encoder PrefixOf('/',file) agrees with live pathlib.Path.is_absolute() on all 4 seeded values. Classification is solver-backed-under-assumptions (not fully-static) precisely because Path.is_absolute() dispatches on os.name; the Windows path string is the one value whose result flips across platforms.
